goal: i wanna change color of my current text
preamble: Colour in Docs isn't a setting you turn on for the document — it's a property carried by individual characters. So the real question isn't "where is the colour control", it's "which characters am I about to repaint". Whatever you have selected right now is the answer. If nothing is selected, Docs holds the colour ready and applies it to the next thing you type.
generalization: Everything in that stretch of the toolbar works the same way: it acts on the selection, and nothing else. Bold, font, size, colour — none of them are document settings, they're properties you paint onto the characters you've highlighted. That's why the habit worth keeping is selecting first and reaching for the toolbar second: the selection is the real instruction, the button is only the paint.

steps.intent: The toolbar holds the controls that change how your selected text looks, and one of them is for the colour of the letters themselves. Clicking it doesn't apply anything yet — it opens a palette, so you can see the choice before you commit to it.
hints: You're changing the appearance of characters, not the structure of the document — so it's in the toolbar, not a menu. Look for the control that shows a colour rather than a word.
Toolbar, in the group with Bold and Italic — the letter A with a coloured bar underneath it.

wrongHints.Highlight color: Easy to mix up, since they sit side by side and both open a palette of colours. That one paints the background behind the text, like a marker pen. You want the one that paints the letters themselves.
wrongHints.Styles: Styles describe what a line of text is — a heading, a subtitle, body text — and the colour comes along as a side effect. Useful when you want every heading to match, but heavy-handed when you only want to recolour what you've selected.
wrongHints.Font: That changes the shape of the letters, not their colour. It's a neighbour in the same toolbar group because both are about appearance, but each one touches a different property.
